questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the final product formed when benzenamine reacts with the given reagents in the sequential order as:
i. (CH_3-$CO )_2$O / Pyridine. \\ ii. Conc. HNO_3$ + H_2$SO_4$ & then reacted with H_3$O$^+$ \\ iii. NaNO_2$ HCl (273K) & then reacted with H_3$PO_2$(aq).$
questions.solution:
Benzenamine (aniline) reacts with acetic anhydride in the presence of pyridine to form acetanilide. This step protects the amino group and prevents polysubstitution and oxidation.

Acetanilide undergoes nitration with a mixture of concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$ and concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to form $p$-nitroacetanilide as the major product due to steric hindrance at the ortho position.

Hydrolysis of $p$-nitroacetanilide with $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$ removes the acetyl group, yielding $p$-nitroaniline.

$p$-Nitroaniline reacts with $\text{NaNO}_2$ and $\text{HCl}$ at $273\text{ K}$ to form $p$-nitrobenzenediazonium chloride.

Reaction of the diazonium salt with aqueous $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$ (hypophosphorous acid) reduces the diazonium group, replacing it with a hydrogen atom (deamination).

The final product formed is nitrobenzene.

Answer: Nitrobenzene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Choose the incorrect statement.
options: Aniline cannot be prepared by Phthalimide reaction
Propan–2–amine can be obtained by reacting acetoxime with Na / C_2$H_5$ OH
The decreasing order of basic strength of amines in aqueous solution is Ethanamine > N,N–Dimethylaniline > Benzenamine
Fluorobenzene cannot be prepared from Benzenediazonium chloride by Sandmeyer's reaction because Fluorination of the Diazonium salt is highly endothermic in nature
questions.solution:
Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is used for the preparation of primary aliphatic amines. Aniline cannot be prepared by this method because aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with the anion formed by phthalimide. Statement A is correct.

Acetoxime is $(CH_3)_2C=NOH$. Reduction of acetoxime with $Na / C_2H_5OH$ yields propan-2-amine, $(CH_3)_2CHNH_2$. Statement B is correct.

Aliphatic amines are more basic than aromatic amines. Among aromatic amines, the $+I$ effect of two methyl groups in N,N-dimethylaniline increases the electron density on nitrogen, making it more basic than benzenamine. Thus, the basic strength order is Ethanamine > N,N-Dimethylaniline > Benzenamine. Statement C is correct.

Fluorobenzene cannot be prepared by Sandmeyer's reaction, but it is prepared by the Balz-Schiemann reaction. The reason it cannot be prepared by Sandmeyer's reaction is not because the fluorination of the diazonium salt is highly endothermic. In fact, direct fluorination is highly exothermic and violent, and $CuF$ is not effective for the Sandmeyer reaction. Therefore, the reason provided in statement D is incorrect.

Answer: Fluorobenzene cannot be prepared from Benzenediazonium chloride by Sandmeyer's reaction because Fluorination of the Diazonium salt is highly endothermic in nature

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
A Nitrogen containing organic compound with molecular formula C$_3$H$_5$N undergoes the following reactions.
C$_3$H$_5$N + Na / Hg in C$_2$H$_5$OH $\rightarrow$ [A]
[A] + CH$_3$COCl / NaOH (aq) $\rightarrow$ [B]
[A] + CHCl$_3$ / KOH on heating $\rightarrow$ [C] (foul smelling compound)
Identify compounds [B] and [C]
questions.solution:
The molecular formula of the given organic compound is $C_3H_5N$. Its degree of unsaturation is $3 + 1 - \dfrac{5}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} = 2$.

The compound undergoes reduction to form [A], which reacts with $CHC$l_3$ and KOH to give a foul-smelling compound [C]. This is the carbylamine reaction, which is characteristic of primary amines. Thus, [A] is a primary amine.

Since [A] is a primary amine obtained by the reduction of a compound with degree of unsaturation 2, the original compound $C_3H_5N$ must be an alkyl cyanide (nitrile). Therefore, $C_3H_5N$ is propanenitrile, $CH_3-CH_2-CN$.

Reduction of propanenitrile with Na/Hg in $C_2H_5OH$ yields propan-1-amine:
$CH_3-CH_2-CN \xrightarrow{Na/Hg, C_2H_5OH} CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-NH_2$ ([A])

Reaction of propan-1-amine [A] with acetyl chloride ($CH_3COCl$) in the presence of NaOH (aq) results in acetylation to form N-propylacetamide:
$CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-NH_2 + CH_3COCl \xrightarrow{NaOH} CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-NH-COCH_3 + HCl$
Thus, [B] is $CH_3-(CH_2)_2-NH-COCH_3$.

Reaction of propan-1-amine [A] with $CHCl_3$ and KOH on heating yields propyl isocyanide, which is the foul-smelling compound:
$CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-NH_2 + CHCl_3 + 3KOH \xrightarrow{$\Delta$} CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-NC + 3KCl + 3H_2O$
Thus, [C] is $CH_3-(CH_2)_2-NC$.

Answer: [B]: CH_3-$(CH_2$)_2-$NH$-$COCH_3$ [C]: CH_3-$(CH_2$)_2-$NC

Identify compounds [B] and [C]

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The reagent used in carbylamine reaction is ----------------------- and the product of the reaction will be ---------------
questions.solution:
The carbylamine reaction is a characteristic test for primary amines (both aliphatic and aromatic).

When a primary amine is heated with chloroform ($\text{CHCl}_3$) and alcoholic potassium hydroxide ($\text{KOH}$), it forms an isocyanide (also known as carbylamine), which has a characteristic foul smell.

The general reaction is:
$R-\text{NH}_2 + \text{CHCl}_3 + 3\text{KOH (alc.)} \xrightarrow{\Delta} R-\text{NC} + 3\text{KCl} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$

Thus, the reagent used is alcoholic $\text{KOH} + \text{CHCl}_3$ and the product is an isocyanide.

Answer: Alcoholic $\text{KOH} + \text{CHCl}_3$ ; isocyanide

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is the correct reaction of Hinsberg's reagent with primary, secondary and tertiary amines?
options: Tertiary amine forms N, N-dialkyl Benzene sulphonamide which is insoluble in alkali
Primary amine forms N-alkyl Benzene sulphonamide which is soluble in alkali
Secondary amine forms N, N-dialkyl Benzene sulphonamide which is soluble in alkali
Primary amine forms N, N-dialkyl Benzene sulphonamide which is soluble in alkali
questions.solution:
Hinsberg's reagent is benzenesulphonyl chloride (C_6H_5SO_2Cl$).

Primary amines react with Hinsberg's reagent to form N-alkylbenzenesulphonamide. The hydrogen attached to the nitrogen in the sulphonamide is strongly acidic due to the presence of the strong electron-withdrawing sulphonyl group. Hence, it is soluble in alkali.

Secondary amines react with Hinsberg's reagent to form N,N-dialkylbenzenesulphonamide. Since N,N-dialkylbenzenesulphonamide does not contain any hydrogen atom attached to the nitrogen atom, it is not acidic and hence insoluble in alkali.

Tertiary amines do not react with Hinsberg's reagent to form sulphonamides.

Therefore, primary amine forms N-alkylbenzenesulphonamide which is soluble in alkali.

Answer: Primary amine forms N-alkyl Benzene sulphonamide which is soluble in alkali$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the correct order of the type of reactions taking place in this sequence:
questions.solution:
Nitrobenzene is converted to Aniline using $Sn/HCl$. This involves the removal of oxygen and addition of hydrogen, which is a Reduction reaction.

Aniline reacts with $NaNO_2/HCl$ (which forms $HNO_2$ in situ) to form Benzene Diazonium Chloride. The process of conversion of a primary aromatic amine into its diazonium salt is called Diazotization.

Benzene Diazonium Chloride reacts with another molecule of aniline in a mildly acidic medium to form $p$-amino Azobenzene. This is an electrophilic aromatic substitution where the diazonium ion acts as an electrophile. This specific type of reaction forming an azo dye is known as a Coupling reaction.

Therefore, the correct sequence of reactions is Reduction, Diazotization, Coupling.

Answer: Reduction, Diazotization, Coupling

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The number of structural isomers possible for a compound with molecular formula $\text{C}_3\text{H}_9\text{N}$ is:
questions.solution:
Degree of unsaturation for $\text{C}_3\text{H}_9\text{N}$ is $3 - \dfrac{9}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} + 1 = 0$.

The compound is a saturated aliphatic amine. It can exist as primary, secondary, or tertiary amines.

Primary amines ($1^{{}^{\circ}}$):
1. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$ (Propan-1-amine)
2. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{NH}_2)\text{CH}_3$ (Propan-2-amine)

Secondary amines ($2^{{}^{\circ}}$):
3. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NHCH}_3$ (N-Methylethanamine)

Tertiary amines ($3^{{}^{\circ}}$):
4. $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{N}$ (N,N-Dimethylmethanamine)

Total number of structural isomers is $4$.

Answer: $4$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the name of the reaction involved in conversion of A→B and name the compound B.$\mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{CN} \xrightarrow[\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}]{$$\mathrm{H}$$^{+}} $$\mathrm{A}$$\cdot \xrightarrow[$$\mathrm{H}^{+}$$/ $$\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}$]{$\mathrm{Cl}$ 2 / $\text{ Red Phosphorous }$} $\mathrm{B}$\)
questions.solution:
Hydrolysis of methyl cyanide in the presence of an acid yields ethanoic acid.

$\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CN} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H}^+ / \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}} \mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{COOH}$ (Compound A)

Ethanoic acid reacts with chlorine in the presence of red phosphorus to give $\alpha$-chloroethanoic acid. This reaction is known as the Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction.

$\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{COOH} \xrightarrow[\mathrm{H}^+ / \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}]{\mathrm{Cl}_2 / \text{Red P}} \mathrm{ClCH}_2\mathrm{COOH}$ (Compound B)

Compound B is 2-chloroethanoic acid.

Answer: Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction, 2-chloro-ethanoic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following compounds
ethanamine (i); diethylamine (ii); aniline (iii) and $N$ - methylbenzenamine (iv) The correct decreasing order of pKb values of the compounds is:
questions.solution:
The basicity of amines is inversely proportional to their $pK_b$ values. Higher basicity corresponds to a lower $pK_b$ value.

Comparing the basicity of the given compounds:
1. Diethylamine (ii) is a secondary aliphatic amine. It is the most basic due to the electron-donating inductive effect of two ethyl groups and favorable solvation.
2. Ethanamine (i) is a primary aliphatic amine. It is less basic than diethylamine due to fewer electron-donating groups.
3. $N$-methylbenzenamine (iv) is an aromatic amine where the lone pair on nitrogen is delocalized into the benzene ring, reducing its availability for protonation. However, the methyl group provides a slight electron-donating effect compared to aniline.
4. Aniline (iii) is a primary aromatic amine where the lone pair is delocalized into the benzene ring. It is the least basic among the given compounds.

The order of basicity is: (ii) > (i) > (iv) > (iii).

Since $pK_b$ is inversely proportional to basicity, the decreasing order of $pK_b$ values is: (iii) > (iv) > (i) > (ii).

Answer: iii $>$ iv $>$ i $>$ ii

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following amines cannot be prepared by Gabriel's phthalimide synthesis?
questions.solution:
Gabriel phthalimide synthesis involves the reaction of potassium phthalimide with an alkyl halide to form an N-alkyl phthalimide, which is subsequently hydrolyzed to yield a primary amine.

The reaction proceeds via an $S_N2$ mechanism. Therefore, the alkyl halide used must be a primary or secondary alkyl halide. Tertiary alkyl halides undergo elimination reactions instead of substitution, and aryl halides do not undergo $S_N2$ reactions with the phthalimide anion.

Analyzing the options:
1. 2-phenylethylamine is a primary amine and can be prepared from 2-phenylethyl chloride.
2. n-propylamine is a primary amine and can be prepared from n-propyl chloride.
3. N-methylbenzylamine is a secondary amine. Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is specifically used for the preparation of primary amines only. It cannot be used to prepare secondary or tertiary amines because the phthalimide anion is a bulky nucleophile and the resulting N-alkyl phthalimide does not allow for further alkylation to form secondary amines.
4. Isobutyl amine is a primary amine and can be prepared from isobutyl chloride.

Thus, N-methylbenzylamine cannot be prepared by this method.

Answer: N-methylbenzylamine

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The major product ' $D$ ' of the following reaction is:
questions.solution:
The starting material is nitrobenzene. Nitrobenzene undergoes electrophilic aromatic substitution with $Cl_{2}/AlCl_{3}$. Since the $-NO_{2}$ group is meta-directing, the chlorine atom enters the meta position, forming A, which is 1-chloro-3-nitrobenzene.

In the next step, A (1-chloro-3-nitrobenzene) is treated with $Zn/HCl$, which is a reducing agent. This reduces the nitro group ($-NO_{2}$) to an amino group ($-NH_{2}$), resulting in B, which is 3-chloroaniline.

Next, B (3-chloroaniline) is treated with $HNO_{2}$ at $0-5^{{}^{\circ}}C$. This is a diazotization reaction, which converts the amino group into a diazonium salt, forming C, which is 3-chlorobenzenediazonium chloride.

Finally, C (3-chlorobenzenediazonium chloride) is treated with $Cu_{2}Br_{2}$ (or $CuBr/HBr$), which is a Sandmeyer reaction. This replaces the diazonium group ($-N_{2}^{+}Cl^{-}$) with a bromine atom, resulting in D, which is 1-bromo-3-chlorobenzene.

Answer: 1-bromo-3-chlorobenzene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Choose the correct statement:
options: Anilinium ion is less resonance stabilised than Aniline.
Aliphatic amines are weaker bases than $\mathrm{NH}_3$ while aromatic amines are stronger bases than $\mathrm{NH}_3$.
Sec-butylamine is optically inactive because Nitrogen atom of the $-\mathrm{NH}_2$ group is achiral.
Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is used for preparing both Ethyl amine and Aniline.
questions.solution:
(1) Correct: In aniline (C_6H_5NH_2$), the lone pair on N is delocalized into the benzene ring, forming multiple resonance structures. In the anilinium ion (C_6H_5NH_3^+$), the lone pair is donated to a proton and can no longer participate in resonance. Hence anilinium ion is less resonance stabilised than aniline.

(2) Incorrect: Aliphatic amines are stronger bases than $NH_3$ due to the $+I$ effect of alkyl groups. Aromatic amines are weaker bases than $NH_3$ because their lone pair is delocalized into the benzene ring.

(3) Incorrect: sec-Butylamine (CH_3CH_2CH(NH_2)CH_3$) has a chiral carbon bonded to four different groups ($-H$, $-CH_3$, $-CH_2CH_3$, $-NH_2$), making it optically active.

(4) Incorrect: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis involves $S_N2$ reaction with alkyl halides. Aryl halides do not undergo $S_N2$, so aniline cannot be prepared by this method.

The correct statement is (1).$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An organic compound $\mathrm{A} \left(\mathrm{C}_{5}  \mathrm{H}$}_{9} $\mathrm{ N}\right) upon reaction with  \mathrm{Na}$/ $\mathrm{Hg}$/ $\mathrm{C}_{2}  \mathrm{H}$}_{5} $\mathrm{OH} gives compound B. B reacts with  \mathrm{NaNO}_{2} /  \mathrm{HCl}$ at 274 K to form C with quantitative liberation of  $\mathrm{N}$}_{2}$ gas. B also reacts with Hinsberg's reagent to form a compound which is soluble in alkali. Identify compound B.$
questions.solution:
Two key reactions of B:

1. Reacts with $NaNO_2/HCl$ at 274 K to liberate $N_2$ quantitatively \Rightarrow characteristic of a primary aliphatic amine (R-NH_2 + HNO_2 \rightarrow R-OH + N_2\uparrow + H_2O$)

2. Reacts with Hinsberg's reagent to form a product soluble in alkali \Rightarrow confirms primary amine (secondary amines give alkali-insoluble product; tertiary amines do not react).

Among the options, only option (3) $ CH_3-(CH_2)_4-NH_2$ is a primary amine. Options (1) and (2) are tertiary and secondary amines respectively, and option (4) is a quaternary ammonium ion.

B is $CH_3-(CH_2)_4-NH_2

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Complete the following 2 reactions A & B by choosing appropriate reactants \([\mathrm{X}]\) & \([\mathrm{Y}]\).
questions.solution:
The reactions shown are electrophilic aromatic substitution reactions, specifically diazo coupling reactions between a diazonium salt and an activated aromatic ring.

In reaction A, benzenediazonium chloride reacts with [X] to form p-hydroxyazobenzene. This is a coupling reaction with phenol ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH}$) in an alkaline medium (indicated by $\text{OH}^{-}$). The phenol acts as the nucleophile, attacking the diazonium cation at the para position.

In reaction B, benzenediazonium chloride reacts with [Y] to form p-dimethylaminoazobenzene. This is a coupling reaction with N,N-dimethylaniline ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{N}(\text{CH}_3)_2$) in an acidic medium (indicated by $\text{H}^{+}$). The dimethylamino group activates the benzene ring towards electrophilic substitution at the para position.

Comparing these with the given options, [X] corresponds to $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH}$ and [Y] corresponds to $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{N}(\text{CH}_3)_2$.

Answer: $[\mathrm{X}] = \mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{OH} \quad [\mathrm{Y}] = \mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{N}(\mathrm{CH}_3)_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An optically active compound $[\mathrm{X}]$ (Molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_8 \mathrm{H}_{11} \mathrm{ N}$ ) reacts with $\mathrm{CHCl}_3$ / Ethanolic KOH on heating to form an isocyanide. On reaction with $\mathrm{NaNO}_2 / \mathrm{HCl}$, it yields an alcohol with liberation of $\mathrm{N}_2$. Identify the compound $[\mathrm{X}]$.
questions.solution:
The molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_8 \mathrm{H}_{11} \mathrm{N}$ corresponds to a degree of unsaturation of $8 - \dfrac{11}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} + 1 = 4$. This indicates the presence of a benzene ring.

The reaction with $\mathrm{CHCl}_3 / \mathrm{KOH}$ (carbylamine test) indicates that $[\mathrm{X}]$ is a primary amine. The reaction with $\mathrm{NaNO}_2 / \mathrm{HCl}$ yielding an alcohol with the liberation of $\mathrm{N}_2$ is characteristic of aliphatic primary amines, as aromatic primary amines form diazonium salts which are stable at low temperatures.

Among the options, 1-phenylethanamine ($\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{NH}_2) \mathrm{CH}_3$) is a primary amine where the amino group is attached to an aliphatic carbon. It contains a chiral center at the carbon atom attached to the amino group, making it optically active. The other options are aromatic amines (anilines), which do not form alcohols under these conditions but rather form stable diazonium salts at $0-5^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$.

Therefore, 1-phenylethanamine satisfies all the given conditions.

Answer: 1-Phenylethanamine.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Two statements, one Assertion and the other Reason are given. Identify the correct option Assertion: Primary and secondary amides on treatment with $\mathrm{Br}_2$ and alcoholic NaOH yield primary and secondary amines respectively and the reaction involves stepping down the series. Reason: The reaction occurs due to the migration of alkyl group from Carbonyl carbon atom to the Nitrogen atom with elimination of carbonyl group as the carbonate salt.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are incorrect.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct.
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct.
questions.solution:
The reaction described is the Hofmann bromamide degradation reaction. In this reaction, a primary amide (RCONH_2$) reacts with $Br_2$ and a strong base (like $NaOH$ or $KOH$) to form a primary amine (RNH_2$) with one carbon atom less than the original amide. This is a well-known method for stepping down the carbon chain.

Secondary amides (RCONHR'$) do not undergo the Hofmann bromamide degradation reaction to yield secondary amines. The reaction is specific to primary amides because it requires two hydrogen atoms on the nitrogen atom to form the intermediate isocyanate (RNCO$) via the migration of the alkyl group. Therefore, the assertion that secondary amides undergo this reaction is incorrect.

The mechanism of the Hofmann bromamide degradation involves the formation of an N-bromamide intermediate, followed by the abstraction of a proton to form an anion, which then undergoes rearrangement. During this rearrangement, the alkyl group migrates from the carbonyl carbon to the nitrogen atom, leading to the formation of an isocyanate (RNCO$), which is subsequently hydrolyzed to the primary amine and carbonate. Thus, the reason correctly describes the mechanism of the reaction for primary amides.

Answer: Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct.$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Choose the correct statement from the options given
options: Benzene diazonium chloride when reacted with Aniline in presence of dil. HCl at 273 K yields $\mathrm{C}_{6} \mathrm{H} 5-  \mathrm{N}=\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{NH}-\mathrm{C}_{6} $$\mathrm{H}_{5}$
On heating an aliphatic primary amine with $\mathrm{CHCl}_{3} in presence of Ethanolic KOH, a Nitrile is formed$
The intermolecular bonding in primary amines is stronger than in secondary amines.
The decreasing order of basic nature of the following amines is: Methylamine \( > \) Dimethylamine \( > \) Trimethylamine \( > \) Aniline.
questions.solution:
(1) Incorrect: Coupling of benzene diazonium chloride with aniline yields p-aminoazobenzene (H_2N-C_6H_4-N=N-C_6H_5$), not the diazoaminobenzene structure shown.

(2) Incorrect: Heating a primary amine with $CHCl_3$ and ethanolic KOH (carbylamine test) yields an isocyanide (carbylamine), not a nitrile.

(3) Correct: Primary amines (R-$NH_2$) have two N-H bonds, enabling a more extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonding network. Secondary amines (R_2NH$) have only one N-H bond, resulting in weaker intermolecular hydrogen bonding.

(4) Incorrect: The correct decreasing order of basic strength in aqueous solution is: Dimethylamine (2°$) > Methylamine (1°$) > Trimethylamine (3°$) > Aniline.

The correct statement is (3).$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
An organic compound $[\mathrm{X}]$ (molecular formula- $\mathrm{C}_5 \mathrm{H}_{11} \mathrm{NO}$ when reacted with $\mathrm{Br}_2 /$ aq. NaOH yielded [Y] which reacts with $\mathrm{CHCl}_3$ and Ethanolic KOH to produce a foul smelling compound.
Compound $[\mathrm{Y}]$ also reacts with HONO to produce Butan-1-ol with liberation of $\mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{ g})$. Identify [X].
questions.solution:
The reaction of compound [X] with $\mathrm{Br}_2 / \mathrm{aq. NaOH}$ is the Hofmann bromamide degradation reaction, which converts an amide ($\mathrm{R-CONH}_2$) into a primary amine ($\mathrm{R-NH}_2$).

The product [Y] reacts with $\mathrm{CHCl}_3$ and ethanolic $\mathrm{KOH}$ to produce a foul-smelling compound (isocyanide test), confirming that [Y] is a primary aliphatic amine.

The reaction of [Y] with $\mathrm{HONO}$ (nitrous acid) produces Butan-1-ol with the liberation of $\mathrm{N}_2$ gas. This indicates that the amine [Y] is Butan-1-amine, $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{NH}_2$.

Since the Hofmann bromamide degradation results in the loss of the carbonyl carbon atom, the original amide [X] must have one more carbon atom than the amine [Y]. Thus, [X] is a pentanamide with the formula $\mathrm{C}_5\mathrm{H}_{11}\mathrm{NO}$.

The structure of the amide corresponding to Butan-1-amine is $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CONH}_2$.

Answer: $\mathrm{CH}_3-\left(\mathrm{CH}_2\right)_3-\mathrm{CONH}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An organic compound with molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_3 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{N}$ on hydrolysis gives compound '$\mathrm{X}$' which on treatment with $\mathrm{Cl}_2 / \mathrm{P}$ gives compound '$\mathrm{Y}$'. Compound '$\mathrm{Y}$' on reaction with $\mathrm{NH}_3$ gives '$\mathrm{Z}$'. The compound '$\mathrm{Z}$' is :
questions.solution:
The molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_3 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{N}$ corresponds to propionitrile ($\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{CN}$).

Hydrolysis of propionitrile ($\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{CN} + 2\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{COOH} + \mathrm{NH}_3$) yields propanoic acid as compound '$\mathrm{X}$'.

Treatment of propanoic acid with $\mathrm{Cl}_2 / \mathrm{P}$ is the Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction, which results in $\alpha$-chlorination: $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{COOH} + \mathrm{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow{\mathrm{P}} \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CHClCOOH}$ (2-chloropropanoic acid) as compound '$\mathrm{Y}$'.

Reaction of 2-chloropropanoic acid with $\mathrm{NH}_3$ involves nucleophilic substitution of the chlorine atom by the amino group: $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CHClCOOH} + 2\mathrm{NH}_3 \rightarrow \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{NH}_2)\mathrm{COOH} + \mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{Cl}$.

The product '$\mathrm{Z}$' is 2-aminopropanoic acid (alanine).

Answer: 2-aminopropanoic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Arrange the following amines in the decreasing order of their solubilities in water.
questions.solution:
The solubility of amines in water depends on their ability to form hydrogen bonds with water molecules. Amines with lower molecular weight and fewer hydrophobic alkyl groups are generally more soluble.

Compound [I] is aniline (C_6H_5NH_2$), which contains a large hydrophobic phenyl group. This large hydrocarbon part significantly reduces its solubility in water.

Compound [II] is ethylamine (CH_3CH_2NH_2$), a primary amine with a small alkyl group. It can form effective hydrogen bonds with water and has a smaller hydrophobic part compared to [I] and [III].

Compound [III] is diethylamine ($(CH_3CH_2)_2NH$), a secondary amine. Although it can form hydrogen bonds, it has two ethyl groups, making it more hydrophobic than ethylamine [II].

Comparing the hydrophobic character: The phenyl group in [I] is the most hydrophobic, followed by the two ethyl groups in [III], and then the single ethyl group in [II].

Therefore, the decreasing order of solubility is ethylamine [II] > diethylamine [III] > aniline [I].

Answer: II > III > I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 4-methyl benzamide (A) on reaction with ethanolic solution of $\mathrm{KOH}$ and bromine gives another compound (B). The compound (B) on treatment with benzoyl chloride gives compound (C). Identify the correct structure of compound (C) from the following.
questions.solution:
The reaction of 4-methylbenzamide with $Br_{2}$ and ethanolic $KOH$ is the Hofmann bromamide degradation reaction. This reaction converts an amide (R-CONH_{2}$) into a primary amine (R-NH_{2}$) with one less carbon atom.

Starting with 4-methylbenzamide (CH_{3}-C_{6}H_{4}-CONH_{2}$), the Hofmann bromamide degradation yields 4-methylaniline (p$-toluidine), which is $CH_{3}-C_{6}H_{4}-NH_{2}$. This is compound (B).

Compound (B), 4-methylaniline, then reacts with benzoyl chloride (C_{6}H_{5}-COCl$) in the presence of a base (like pyridine or aqueous $NaOH$) to form an amide through a nucleophilic acyl substitution reaction. This is the Schotten-Baumann reaction.

The reaction is: $CH_{3}-C_{6}H_{4}-NH_{2} + C_{6}H_{5}-COCl \rightarrow CH_{3}-C_{6}H_{4}-NH-CO-C_{6}H_{5} + HCl$.

The resulting product (C) is $N$-(4-methylphenyl)benzamide, which corresponds to the structure where the nitrogen atom is attached to the 4-methylphenyl group and the carbonyl group of the benzoyl moiety. This matches the first structure provided in the options.

Answer: $

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: One of the reactions A, B, C, D given below yields a product which will not answer Hinsberg's test when reacted with Benzene sulphonyl chloride. Identify the reaction.
questions.solution:
Hinsberg test is used to distinguish between primary, secondary, and tertiary amines. Benzene sulphonyl chloride ($C_{6}H_{5}SO_{2}Cl$) reacts with primary and secondary amines to form sulfonamides. Primary amines form N-alkylbenzenesulfonamides which are soluble in alkali, while secondary amines form N,N-dialkylbenzenesulfonamides which are insoluble in alkali. Tertiary amines do not react with benzene sulphonyl chloride because they lack an acidic hydrogen atom on the nitrogen.

Reaction [A]: Benzamide ($C_{6}H_{5}CONH_{2}$) reacts with $LiAlH_{4}$ to form benzylamine ($C_{6}H_{5}CH_{2}NH_{2}$), which is a primary amine and gives a positive Hinsberg test.

Reaction [B]: $p$-Nitrobenzonitrile ($NO_{2}-C_{6}H_{4}-CN$) reacts with $Na/Hg$ in $C_{2}H_{5}OH$ (Bouveault-Blanc reduction conditions) to reduce the nitrile group to a primary amine ($CH_{2}NH_{2}$), which gives a positive Hinsberg test.

Reaction [C]: $m$-Tolunitrile ($CH_{3}-C_{6}H_{4}-CN$) reacts with $H_{2}/Ni$ to form $m$-methylbenzylamine ($CH_{3}-C_{6}H_{4}-CH_{2}NH_{2}$), which is a primary amine and gives a positive Hinsberg test.

Reaction [D]: Benzonitrile ($C_{6}H_{5}CN$) reacts with $SnCl_{2}/HCl$ followed by hydrolysis (Stephen reduction) to form benzaldehyde ($C_{6}H_{5}CHO$). Benzaldehyde is an aldehyde and does not contain an amino group, so it does not react with benzene sulphonyl chloride and thus will not answer the Hinsberg test.

Answer: D

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A compound having molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_4 \mathrm{H}_{11} \mathrm{N}$, reacts with $\mathrm{CHCl}_3$ in alcoholic $\mathrm{KOH}$, on heating, to form a compound with a foul smell. Identify the optically active isomer of the compound which also shows the above reaction.
questions.solution:
The reaction of a compound with $\mathrm{CHCl}_3$ and alcoholic $\mathrm{KOH}$ to produce a foul-smelling substance (isocyanide) is the carbylamine test. This test is specific to primary amines (R-NH_2$).

The molecular formula \mathrm{C}_4 \mathrm{H}_{11} \mathrm{N}$ corresponds to a saturated primary amine. The possible primary amine isomers are:
1. Butan-1-amine: $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{NH}_2$
2. Butan-2-amine: $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{NH}_2)-\mathrm{CH}_3$
3. 2-Methylpropan-1-amine: $(\mathrm{CH}_3)_2\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{NH}_2$
4. 2-Methylpropan-2-amine: $(\mathrm{CH}_3)_3\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{NH}_2$

Among these, we check for optical activity. A molecule is optically active if it contains a chiral center (a carbon atom bonded to four different groups).

In Butan-2-amine, the carbon at position 2 is bonded to a methyl group, an ethyl group, a hydrogen atom, and an amino group. Since all four groups are distinct, this carbon is chiral. Therefore, Butan-2-amine is optically active.

Answer: Butan-2-amine

questions.solution:
Toluene reacts with conc. $HNO_{3}$ and $H_{2}SO_{4}$ (nitrating mixture) to undergo electrophilic aromatic substitution. Since the methyl group is ortho/para directing, the major product [B] is p-nitrotoluene.

Reduction of p-nitrotoluene with $Fe/HCl$ converts the nitro group ($-NO_{2}$) into an amino group ($-NH_{2}$), yielding [C], which is p-toluidine (4-methylaniline).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which one of the following shows the correct increasing order of basic nature of the given compounds?
A: Phenylmethanamine
B: N-Ethylethanamine
C:N, N-Dimethylaniline
D : N, N-Dimethylmethanamine
questions.solution:
The basicity of amines depends on the availability of the lone pair on the nitrogen atom. Electron-donating groups increase basicity, while electron-withdrawing groups or resonance delocalization decrease it.

Compound A is Phenylmethanamine ($C_{6}H_{5}CH_{2}NH_{2}$), a primary amine where the lone pair is not delocalized into the ring, but the phenyl group exerts a weak inductive effect. It is more basic than aromatic amines but less basic than aliphatic amines.

Compound B is N-Ethylethanamine ($(C_{2}H_{5})_{2}NH$), a secondary aliphatic amine. Secondary aliphatic amines are generally the most basic due to the strong inductive effect of two alkyl groups and favorable solvation.

Compound C is N,N-Dimethylaniline ($C_{6}H_{5}N(CH_{3})_{2}$), a tertiary aromatic amine. The lone pair on the nitrogen is delocalized into the benzene ring, making it the least basic among the given compounds.

Compound D is N,N-Dimethylmethanamine ($(CH_{3})_{3}N$), a tertiary aliphatic amine. While it has three electron-donating methyl groups, its basicity is often lower than secondary amines due to steric hindrance and solvation effects in aqueous media.

Comparing the basicity: C (aromatic) < A (primary aliphatic/aromatic-like) < D (tertiary aliphatic) < B (secondary aliphatic).

Thus, the increasing order is C < A < D < B.

Answer: C < A < D < B

questions.q:
Aniline undergoes reactions with reagents given in the order shown
(i) Aqueous $\mathrm{Br}_2$
(ii) $\mathrm{NaNO}_2 / \mathrm{HCl} / 0^0 \mathrm{C}$
(iii) Hypophosphorous acid
What is the product formed at the end of these reactions?
questions.solution:
Aniline reacts with aqueous $\text{Br}_2$ to form $2,4,6$-tribromoaniline as the major product due to the strong activating effect of the $-\text{NH}_2$ group.

The $2,4,6$-tribromoaniline then reacts with $\text{NaNO}_2 / \text{HCl}$ at $0^{{}^{\circ}}\text{C}$ to undergo diazotization, forming the corresponding diazonium salt, $2,4,6$-tribromobenzenediazonium chloride.

Finally, the reaction of the diazonium salt with hypophosphorous acid ($\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$) and water results in the reduction of the diazonium group to a hydrogen atom, yielding $1,3,5$-tribromobenzene as the final product.

Answer: $1,3,5$ - Tribromobenzene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following will give a positive result when it is warmed with Chloroform and alcoholic solution of $\mathrm{KOH}$ ?
questions.solution:
The carbylamine reaction is a characteristic test for primary amines. When a primary amine is heated with chloroform (CHCl_3$) and an alcoholic solution of potassium hydroxide (KOH$), an isocyanide (carbylamine) is formed, which is characterized by an extremely foul smell.

The reaction is represented as: $R-NH_2 + CHCl_3 + 3KOH \rightarrow R-NC + 3KCl + 3H_2O$.

Analyzing the given options:
(1) p-Methylbenzylamine is a primary amine (CH_3-C_6H_4-CH_2-NH_2$), so it will undergo the carbylamine reaction.
(2) N-Methyl-o-Methylaniline is a secondary amine (CH_3-C_6H_4-NH-CH_3$), which does not give the carbylamine test.
(3) N-Methyl-p-Methylaniline is a secondary amine (CH_3-C_6H_4-NH-CH_3$), which does not give the carbylamine test.
(4) N,N-Dimethylaniline is a tertiary amine (C_6H_5-N(CH_3)_2$), which does not give the carbylamine test.

Therefore, only p-Methylbenzylamine gives a positive result.

Answer: p-Methylbenzylamine

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Select the strongest base from the given compounds:
[A] p- $\mathrm{NO}_2-\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_4 \mathrm{NH}_2$
[B] $\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{NH}_2$
[C] $\mathrm{m}-\mathrm{NO}_2-\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_4 \mathrm{NH}_2$
[D] $\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{NH}_2$
questions.solution:
The basicity of amines is determined by the availability of the lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom for protonation.

In p-nitroaniline [A] and m-nitroaniline [C], the $-\mathrm{NO}_2$ group is a strong electron-withdrawing group (EWG) that decreases the electron density on the nitrogen atom through both inductive (-I) and resonance (-M) effects, significantly reducing basicity compared to aniline [D].

In aniline [D], the lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom is in conjugation with the benzene ring, which decreases its availability for protonation.

In benzylamine [B], the $-\mathrm{NH}_2$ group is attached to a $-\mathrm{CH}_2-$ group, which is attached to the benzene ring. The $-\mathrm{CH}_2-$ group acts as an insulator, preventing the lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen from being delocalized into the benzene ring via resonance. Consequently, benzylamine behaves like an aliphatic amine and is significantly more basic than aniline and its derivatives.

Answer: [B]

The reaction of a nitrile (R-CN$) with a Grignard reagent (R'-MgX$) followed by acidic hydrolysis (H_3O^{+}$) is a standard method for the synthesis of ketones.

The mechanism proceeds as follows:
1. The nucleophilic alkyl group (CH_3^{-}$) from the Grignard reagent attacks the electrophilic carbon of the nitrile group ($-CN$).
2. This forms an imine salt intermediate: $Ar-C(CH_3)=N-MgBr$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Gabriel's synthesis is used frequency for the preparation of which of the following?
questions.solution: Gabriel's phthalimide synthesis is used to prepare pure primary (1°$) amines. Phthalimide is treated with KOH to form potassium phthalimide, which reacts with a primary alkyl halide via $S_N2$, followed by hydrolysis (or hydrazinolysis) to release the primary amine. This method avoids over-alkylation (formation of 2°$ and $3°$ amines) that occurs when $NH_3$ reacts directly with alkyl halides.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is highly basic?
questions.solution:
The basicity of amines is determined by the availability of the lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom for protonation.

In aniline, the lone pair on the nitrogen atom is involved in resonance with the benzene ring, which decreases its availability for protonation, making it weakly basic.

In diphenylamine, the lone pair on the nitrogen atom is involved in resonance with two benzene rings, which further decreases its availability compared to aniline, making it even less basic.

In triphenylamine, the lone pair on the nitrogen atom is involved in resonance with three benzene rings, making it extremely weakly basic or essentially non-basic.

In benzylamine (C_{6}H_{5}CH_{2}NH_{2}$), the lone pair on the nitrogen atom is not involved in resonance with the benzene ring because the nitrogen is separated from the ring by a $CH_{2}$ group. The electron-donating inductive effect of the benzyl group increases the electron density on the nitrogen atom, making it significantly more basic than the aromatic amines listed.

Answer: Benzylamine$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is most stable?
questions.solution:
Stability of diazonium salts (R-N_2^+X^-$) depends on the stability of the carbocation formed after loss of $N_2$.

$CH_2N_2^+X^-$ and $CH_3CH_2N_2^+X^-$: aliphatic \Rightarrow resulting carbocations are highly unstable. These decompose rapidly.

$ C_6H_5CH_2N_2^+X^-$: benzyl carbocation is resonance stabilized, but still relatively reactive.

$C_6H_5N_2^+X^-$: the diazonium group is directly attached to the aromatic ring. The lone pair on the nitrogen delocalizes into the ring \Rightarrow the diazonium cation itself is resonance stabilized. This makes benzene diazonium salt the most stable, existing in solution at 0-5^{}^{\circ} C$.

Correct option: (2)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The correct increasing order of basic strength of following amines,
$\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{5} \mathrm{NH}_{2}, \mathrm{NH}_{3},\left(\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{5}\right)_{2} \mathrm{NH}_{6} \mathrm{C}_{6} \mathrm{H}_{5} \mathrm{NH}_{2}$ in gaseous state is
questions.solution:
Aniline is less basic than ammonia and aliphatic amines due to delocalisation of lone pair of electrons on the benzene ring.
Aliphatic amines are stronger bases, than ammonia due to $+I$-effect of alkyl group. More the number of alkyl groups stronger is the base.
Hence, basic strength will follow the following order $\left(\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{5}\right)_{2} \mathrm{NH} \gt \mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{5} \mathrm{NH}_{2} \gt \mathrm{NH}_{3} \gt \mathrm{C}_{6} \mathrm{H}_{5} \mathrm{NH}_{2}$
